quote: Well, so it's been winter. We just bought the house, Two months ago,
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a live anchor — a brand-new home, currently gas-heavy, with an unknown summer electric load once AC kicks in ('with summertime, I don't know how high it'll be'). The rep acknowledges warmly but files it as small talk rather than reflecting it back as forward-pulling curiosity about how much the bill could grow.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that with the appointment already trending toward a book, deepening the bill discussion risked slowing an efficient call — but the anchor was free value that costs seconds to use.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to mirror numbers like this back to the customer: a one-line 'so once you're running AC this summer, that PSO bill's the number we really want to watch' would have planted curiosity going into the closer's call at no cost to call length.

quote: Sounds good. Well, yeah, that's pretty much all the questions we have here for you.
stewart_read: The rep closes out verify very quickly — the interest-in-solar answer (advertisement + cost fear) got one acknowledging line and no follow-up, and the bill range ($100-200, described by the customer himself as unreliable due to winter/gas heat) wasn't probed for the more telling summer figure. This is a verify-depth gap, not scope creep — the rep never over-explained product, he simply didn't deepen the two anchor questions the schema flags as highest-value (interest reason and bill).
alternative_hypothesis: The call was already running efficiently and the rep may have judged additional probing unnecessary given the customer was cooperative and the appointment was clearly heading to a book — a legitimate efficiency trade-off on a short, non-hostile call.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on depth vs. speed: the verify_completion_threshold is about quality of the anchor answers, not just checking the box. A 10-15 second follow-up on the bill or interest reason costs little and gives the closer a sharper anchor to open with.

quote: Well, that's been my biggest concern is I always heard how expensive it was to for the panels and the batteries and all the things.
stewart_read: This is the customer's own opening objection repeating verbatim in spirit at the very end of the call, after the appointment is already locked. coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close the loop on a recurring objection with a short callback line ('exactly why the no-out-of-pocket piece we talked about earlier matters here') rather than a generic reassurance, so the customer heads into the specialist call without the same fear still active.

coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always run the full button-up checklist (hour block, no driving, computer access) even on easy, cooperative calls — the schema ties this specifically to no-show rate, not to customer difficulty.
